newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan central bank injects T$8.59 bln in funds.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan central bank injects T$8.59 bln in funds.

text.p: Taiwan's central bank, reacting as money rates sizzled in double digits, on Monday injected T$8.59 billion worth of funds into the banking system through open market operations, a central bank official said.

The bank, in direct deals with financial institutions, purchased back T$8.59 billion in negotiable certificates of deposit, commercial paper or government bonds offered by financial institutions with a single yield at 9.0 percent, the official said.
The institutions have the option of repurchasing the instruments within four days of their issue, the official said.
Taiwan's interbank rate has persisted at double-digit levels in recent days, creating tight liquidity in the banking system as funds continued to stream out of banks into the red-hot stock market.
In a departure from previous practice, the central bank demanded that financial institutions submit reports explaining their capital flows.
Analysts said the move aimed to prevent any of the newly released liquidity from flowing into the red-hot stock market.

The overnight interbank rate, which had closed higher for 11 consecutive sessions, had eased to 10.345 percent at midday on Monday from Saturday's record-high 11.325 finish -- but still was roughly double the central bank's target zone of 5.0-5.5.
The central bank said it would continue to watch closely the banking system's liquidity flows.
